blocks.why: Day off, but tomorrow is a 06:10 report — bed at 21:00 local so the 04:30 alarm isn't stealing from an empty tank.
Second early in a row and an even earlier alarm (03:30 local), so straight to bed after the four-sector day.
This afternoon sleep is my real sleep for the ARN night — curtains shut, phone off, home by 12:30 and down by 12:45 local.
Straight to bed off the all-nighter; six hours is all I'll get before the 19:10 report, so protect it hard.
Home just after 01:00 local from FRA — proper night sleep before a 12-hour day that finishes near midnight.
Wind-down sleep into the day off, but kept to seven hours so I can still get to bed early tonight.
Forty-minute top-up on the day off to insure the short night before a 04:00 local alarm.
Early night for the 05:40 report — I know 20:30 local is a hard sell, hence the nap this afternoon.
Off the longest duty of the month on a dawn wake — let the alarm off and sleep the full ten hours.
An hour down before the late — the BCN turn lands at 02:26 local and that nap is what flies it.
Home just before 04:00 local; six hours only, so I'm still tired enough to go to bed early tonight for the 05:05.
Afternoon nap to bridge the gap between the short lie-in and an evening bedtime.
Bed at 19:45 local for a 03:30 alarm — the last night off before three duties in three days.
Half an hour on landing home to take the edge off, short enough not to spoil tonight.
Nine hours banked ahead of the sim — this is the only proper night I get before the 02:00 report on the 12th.
Straight home from the sim and into bed at 17:30 local — awkward hour, but it's the whole rest before a 02:00 report.
Blackout blinds and earplugs — I've just done one night and I'm about to do a second, so this six and a half hours is non-negotiable.
Recovery sleep off two nights back to back; wake by 17:00 local so I can still sleep tonight.
First real night of the four days off — get the body clock back on London time.
Normal nights on days off, same times every day, no lie-ins.
Keeping the rhythm — the sleep debt from the 12th takes about three nights to clear.
Full night before the late report; no need to get up early tomorrow.
Hour down late morning — I won't be in bed again until gone 03:00 local after the ARN turn.
Home about 03:00 local; cap it at six and a half hours because I'm back up before 04:00 tomorrow.
Afternoon nap on the day off to make the early bedtime survivable.
Bed at 20:30 local for the 05:40 — turning a night finish into an early start in one day off is the hardest ask of the month.
Short nap on getting home, finished by 14:00 local so tonight's early bedtime still works.
Third early in the block — in bed by 20:00 local, alarm 03:30.
Short duty done by mid-morning — an hour's nap clears the accumulated early-start debt.
Nine hours with a midday report tomorrow — this is the catch-up night after three earlies.
Normal night into the day off.
Thirty minutes on the day off as insurance against a short night before the 06:10.
Bed at 21:00 local — tomorrow is a thirteen-hour day out of an early report, and it starts here.
Off the FCO day and into four days off — sleep as long as it comes.
Steady nights on the days off.
Steady nights, and start pulling the bedtime earlier for the 28th.
Half an hour earlier again — walking the body clock back rather than jumping it.
Afternoon nap before the last early-start block.
Bed at 20:30 local for the 03:30 alarm and the 05:05 report.
Forty-five minutes on getting home after a ten-and-a-half hour day off an early — nothing longer, I want tonight.
Long night with a lunchtime report tomorrow — bank it before two late finishes.
Nap before the 13:15 report — the DUB leg lands at 23:07 local and I want to be sharp for it.
Home just after midnight; a full night is fine with a 15:25 report.
Last duty of the roster done by 20:31 local — normal night, back on London time for whatever October brings.

conflicts.statement: Two duties on the same date: a 04:05Z report finishing 10:28Z, then a report at 20:30Z for an all-night ARN/CDG run. The only sleep opportunity is an afternoon one, taken on a body clock that has already been awake since 03:30 local and at a time of day when sleep is shallow and short.
options: Treat 12:45–17:30 local as a duty in itself — blackout, earplugs, phone off, no errands, no driving beyond the commute
Ask crewing whether the morning DUB/BCN turn can be dropped so the night duty is entered fresh
Plan controlled rest in the cruise on LY798 and LY422 with the other pilot, and brief it before push
Arrange a lift or a cab home at 09:07 local so no driving happens on the far side of the night

conflicts.statement: The night duty ends 08:07Z on 09-04 and the next report is 18:10Z the same day — about 10 hours off duty, of which roughly 2 hours go to commuting, leaving a ~6h recovery sleep taken in daylight after a whole night awake.
options: Sleep 09:15–15:30Z and do not set the alarm any earlier than 15:30Z
Ask for the 09-04 FRA turn to be moved to another crew — it is the third body-clock reversal in 48 hours
Report fatigued if the afternoon sleep does not happen; the LY879 sector lands at 23:20Z

conflicts.statement: Reports of 05:10Z on 09-02 and 04:05Z on 09-03 back to back. Sleep before an early start is always short — realistically 6.5–7 hours each night even with a disciplined 20:00-21:00 local bedtime — so a sleep debt is already building before the 09-03 night duty.
options: Start pulling bedtime earlier from 08-31, not from 09-01
Accept a shorter 09-02 evening (bed 20:00 local) and add a nap on 09-03 afternoon as planned
Ask whether the 09-02 and 09-03 earlies can be swapped so one of them is a later report

conflicts.statement: The simulator finishes 15:00Z on 09-11 and the next report is 01:00Z on 09-12 — under 10 hours, of which ~2 hours is commuting. The whole rest has to be taken as an evening sleep starting around 17:30 local, which lands squarely in the wake-maintenance zone when the body is least able to fall asleep.
options: Bank sleep the night before: 20:00Z on 09-10 to 05:00Z on 09-11, nine hours
Ask crewing to release the 09-12 02:00 local report — a sim day followed by a WOCL-spanning duty is a poor pairing
Go straight home from the sim, no debrief drinks, curtains shut and in bed by 17:30 local
If the evening sleep does not come, call fatigued before leaving home rather than at report

conflicts.statement: Highest-risk item of the roster. Duty A reports 01:00Z and works straight through the WOCL to 11:35Z. After ~10 hours off, Duty B reports 21:35Z and runs 13h04 through a second consecutive WOCL, with four sectors and the last approach into LHR at 10:09Z on 09-13 after roughly 30 hours of heavily disrupted sleep.
options: Push crewing hard to break the pair — one of these two duties should go to another crew
If both are flown, protect 13:00–19:30Z on 09-12 as blackout sleep and take nothing less
Brief planned controlled rest on both the BCN and ARN sectors of Duty B
Do not drive home on 09-13 — book a cab or a hotel room at the airport
File a fatigue report regardless of outcome so the pairing is visible to the operator

conflicts.statement: The 09-17 duty lands at 00:37Z and finishes 01:07Z on 09-18. A single day off then precedes a 04:40Z report on 09-19, requiring the body clock to move roughly eight hours earlier in about 28 hours.
options: Cap the 09-18 morning sleep at 08:30Z, nap 14:00–14:45Z, and be in bed by 19:30Z
Ask whether the 09-19 BCN turn can be exchanged for a later report
Expect a short night on 09-18 and treat the 09-19 duty as a low-alertness day: extra cross-checks, no rushed turnrounds

conflicts.statement: Reports of 04:40Z, 04:05Z and 11:20Z on 09-19, 09-20 and 09-21, all following the night finish on 09-18. Three consecutive duty days with wake-ups before 04:00 local build cumulative debt even though each individual duty is short.
options: Use the 09-20 late-morning finish for a genuine one-hour nap, then a nine-hour night into the 09-21 midday report
Keep bedtime fixed at 20:00 local across 09-18 and 09-19 rather than drifting later
Flag to crewing that the block is the tail of a night duty, not a fresh start

conflicts.statement: 12h55 duty reporting 05:10Z (04:30 local wake), four sectors including the FCO turn, finishing 18:05Z. Alertness at the top of descent into LHR will be running on a 14-hour continuous wake plus a short pre-early night.
options: Bed at 21:00 local on 09-22 with a short afternoon nap that day to protect it
Split the flying with the other pilot so the FCO return is not flown by whoever also flew the FRA turn
Eat and hydrate on the FCO ground time rather than pushing through

conflicts.statement: No unreadable entries. For the record: the roster prints local/Zulu pairs and every line reconciles against block time with LHR and DUB at UTC+1 and BCN, CDG, FRA, ARN and FCO at UTC+2, and a uniform 60-minute report offset on flying duties. The 09-11 SIM is taken as a stated 07:00Z start with no offset. Duties are filed under their report date, so 09-03 and 09-12 each carry two entries.
options: Confirm with crewing that the 09-11 sim brief is at 08:00 local and not earlier
Confirm the report offset is 60 minutes and not 65 or 75 for the four-sector days
